# mk_sizer

> Flutter package for responsive/adaptive sizing. Wrap the app in `MKSizer`, pick
> a design size (default `360x690`, the Figma/XD frame the numbers below were
> designed against), then scale any number against the current screen with
> extension getters like `.w`, `.h`, `.r`, `.sp`, and `.mkGap`.

Package name: `mk_sizer`. Import with `package:mk_sizer/mk_sizer.dart`.
Repository: https://github.com/kishormainali/mk_sizer
Pub: https://pub.dev/packages/mk_sizer

All extensions/widgets below scale 1:1 (no-op) until an `MKSizer` has built at
least once above them in the tree, so they are always safe to call.

## Setup

Wrap the root of the app (or any subtree) in `MKSizer`:

```dart
MKSizer(
  builder: (context) {
    return MaterialApp(home: HomePage());
  },
);
```

- `designSize` (default `Size(360, 690)`): the reference size the numeric
  literals below are authored against. Pass a different `Size` to match your
  Figma/XD frame.
- `rebuildOnChange` (default `true`): rebuilds the whole subtree when the
  available size changes (rotation, window resize) so `10.w`-style extensions
  stay correct even inside `const` widgets. Set `false` and use the
  `context.w/h/r/sp/pw/ph` methods instead for narrower, per-widget rebuilds
  (those are not tracked when `rebuildOnChange` is `false`).

- `respectAspectRatio` (default `false`): blends the width/height scales toward
  their mean as the device aspect ratio diverges from `designSize`'s, reducing
  stretch on e.g. tablets. No-op when aspect ratios match.
- `minScaleFactor` / `maxScaleFactor`: clamp `.w`/`.h`/`.r` scales (applied
  with `respectAspectRatio`).
- `minTextScaleFactor` / `maxTextScaleFactor`: clamp the `.sp` scale
  independently of layout scales (always applied; `context.sp` too).

## Responsive builder (`lib/src/mk_responsive_builder.dart`)

- `MKResponsiveBuilder(mobile:, smallMobile:, tablet:, desktop:)` picks a
  builder by `MediaQuery` width (breakpoints 360 / 600 / 1024, overridable);
  missing tiers fall back to the next-smaller tier, ultimately `mobile`.
- `context.deviceType` returns an `MKDeviceType`.
- `context.resValue(mobile: .., tablet: .., desktop: ..)` picks a value the
  same way.

## Core `num` extensions (`MKSizeExt`, in `lib/src/mk_extension.dart`)

Call these on any `num` literal, e.g. `20.w`, `15.sp`.

- `.w` — scales by `screenWidth / designSize.width`. Use for widths.
- `.h` — scales by `screenHeight / designSize.height`. Use for heights.
- `.r` — scales by `min(widthScale, heightScale)`. Use for anything that
  should stay uniform regardless of aspect ratio (radii, icon sizes, uniform
  padding).
- `.sp` — scales by the width scale (same as `.w`). Use for font sizes.
- `.pw` — `this * screenWidth` (percentage-of-screen-width helper).
- `.ph` — `this * screenHeight` (percentage-of-screen-height helper).
- `.verticalSpace` — `SizedBox(height: this.h)`.
- `.verticalSpaceRadius` — `SizedBox(height: this.r)`.
- `.horizontalSpace` — `SizedBox(width: this.w)`.
- `.horizontalSpaceRadius` — `SizedBox(width: this.r)`.
- `.mkGap` — a responsive, axis-aware gap widget (`MKGap`, see below);
  `10.mkGap` inside a `Row`/`Column`. Named `mkGap` rather than `gap` to avoid
  colliding with other packages' `num` extensions of the same name (e.g.
  `fp_extensions`, which depends on `package:gap`).
- `.mkSliverGap` — the sliver equivalent of `.mkGap` (`MKSliverGap`, see
  below); `10.mkSliverGap` inside a `CustomScrollView`'s `slivers:`.

## Responsive gap (`MKGap`, in `lib/src/mk_gap.dart`)

`10.mkGap` returns an `MKGap`, a self-contained reimplementation of
`package:gap`'s `Gap` (no dependency on that package). It inspects its actual
`RenderFlex` parent at layout time to detect whether it sits in a `Row`
(horizontal) or `Column`/`Flex` (vertical) — or a `Scrollable`'s
`axisDirection` as a fallback when there is no direct `Flex` ancestor — and
scales the value accordingly:

- Horizontal parent → scaled with the same logic as `.w`.
- Vertical parent → scaled with the same logic as `.h`.
- Neither detected → falls back to `.r`.

So the same `10.mkGap` call is correct whether it ends up between `Row` or
`Column` children, without needing a `.w`/`.h` suffix. Construct it directly
as `MKGap(10)` if you're not chaining off a numeric literal.

`MKGap` mirrors `package:gap`'s full API surface via named constructors:

- `MKGap(value, {crossAxisExtent, color})` — the base gap; `crossAxisExtent`
  (optional) is scaled on the opposite axis and defaults to `0`.
- `MKGap.expand(value, {color})` — like `Gap.expand`: fills the cross axis.
- `MKGap.max(value, {crossAxisExtent, color})` — like `MaxGap`: wraps itself
  in a `Flexible` so it takes at most `value`, shrinking if the parent `Flex`
  doesn't have enough room.
- `MKGap.maxExpand(value, {color})` — like `MaxGap.expand`: combines both.

Constraint (inherited from the `gap` package's design): the non-`.max`
variants must be a direct-ish descendant of a `Row`/`Column`/`Flex` — only
`StatelessWidget`s or `StatefulWidget`s may sit between it and that `Flex` —
or a descendant of a `Scrollable`. Otherwise it throws `FlutterError` at
layout time. `.max`/`.maxExpand` must sit directly inside a `Flex` (they wrap
themselves in `Flexible`, like `MaxGap`).

## Responsive sliver gap (`MKSliverGap`, in `lib/src/mk_sliver_gap.dart`)

`10.mkSliverGap` returns an `MKSliverGap`, the sliver equivalent of `MKGap`
(matching `package:gap`'s `SliverGap`) for use as a direct child of a sliver
list — e.g. inside a `CustomScrollView`'s `slivers:`. Unlike `MKGap`, it
doesn't need a `RenderFlex`/`Scrollable` ancestor to detect its axis: a
sliver's `SliverConstraints.axis` always tells it directly, so it scales with
`.w` when that axis is horizontal and `.h` when vertical.

## `EdgeInsets` extension (`MKEdgeInsetsX`, in `lib/src/mk_extension.dart`)

Call these on an existing `EdgeInsets` to scale every side:

- `.r` — scales all four sides with `.r`.
- `.w` — scales all four sides with `.w`.
- `.h` — scales all four sides with `.h`.
- `.wh` — scales `left`/`right` with `.w` and `top`/`bottom` with `.h`.

## Responsive `EdgeInsets` constructors (`lib/src/mk_edgeinsets.dart`)

Drop-in, pre-scaled replacements for `EdgeInsets`/`EdgeInsetsDirectional`
constructors — pass raw design-space numbers, the scaling happens inside the
constructor. Left/right/start/end scale with `.w`, top/bottom with `.h`
(`all` uses `.r`).

`MKPadding(padding:, child:)` is a `Padding` with a `const` constructor that
scales horizontal insets with `.w` and vertical insets with `.h` and re-scales
on size change, e.g.
`const MKPadding(padding: EdgeInsets.all(16), child: ...)`.

`MKSizedBox({width, height, child})` is a `SizedBox` with a `const` constructor
that scales `width` with `.w` and `height` with `.h` and re-scales on size
change.

## Context-based sizing (`MKContextX`, in `lib/src/mk_model.dart`)

Alternative to the `num` extensions that reads scale factors from an
`InheritedModel` (`MKSizerModel`) instead of a global singleton. Prefer this
with `MKSizer.rebuildOnChange: false`: each call site only rebuilds when the
specific aspect it depends on (width/height/text) changes, rather than the
whole subtree rebuilding on every resize.

- `context.w(num v)`
- `context.h(num v)`
- `context.r(num v)` — depends on both width and height aspects.
- `context.sp(num v)`
- `context.pw(num v)`
- `context.ph(num v)`

Throws `FlutterError` if called with no `MKSizer` above the context in the
tree (whereas the `num` extensions above degrade to 1:1 instead of throwing).

## Notes for generating code against this package

- Prefer the `num` extensions (`.w`, `.h`, `.r`, `.sp`, `.mkGap`, …) for
  typical UI code; reach for `context.*` only when the caller explicitly
  wants narrower rebuilds and has set `rebuildOnChange: false`.
- Use `.sp` for font sizes, `.r` for radii/icon sizes/anything meant to look
  the same regardless of aspect ratio, `.w`/`.h` for explicit
  width/height dimensions, and `.mkGap` for spacing between `Row`/`Column`
  children instead of a manually-axed `SizedBox`.
- Don't wrap the same numeric literal in both a `num` extension and
  `MKEdgeInsets`/`MKEdgeInsetsDirectional` — those constructors already scale
  their arguments internally.
